items.title: 4.3 Combining Computational Structures for Complex Problems

source_refs.note: Topic 4.3 (PDF 118, printed 115). Long question 8 is answered.

blocks.text: Combining lists, stacks, queues, trees and graphs is essential for complex problems: each has its own strengths, and together they give stronger, more efficient solutions that manage complex relationships and fit specific needs.

blocks.prompt: Consider organizing a desk. How could a stack and a queue both help (long question 8)?
blocks.explanation: Keep the jobs, sort papers, put away books and clean the desk, in a queue so they are done in the order planned. Papers pile up as a stack: the last paper placed on top is the first one picked up and filed, and books can be stacked and shelved from the top down. The queue fixes the order of tasks; the stack handles the items inside each task.

items: Combining structures uses each one's strengths for complex problems.
